title: Continuatio Fragmentorum ex Adversariis mathematicis depromptorum

deep.reconstruction:
Problem: find two surfaces that can be carried one onto the other so that corresponding points keep their mutual distances. In modern terms, find pairs of isometric (applicable) surfaces.

Euler parametrizes both surfaces by the same two independent parameters (r,s): X(r,s)=(t,u,v) and Y(r,s)=(x,y,z). He considers the infinitesimal triangle formed by Z, the point Z+X_r dr and the point Z+X_s ds. He computes its squared sides:
- Zr² = |X_r|² dr²
- Zs² = |X_s|² ds²
- rs² = |X_r dr − X_s ds|² = Zr² + Zs² − 2 dr ds (X_r·X_s)

The triangle must be congruent on both surfaces. This gives E = E', G = G', F = F', i.e. equality of the first fundamental forms in a common parametrization. Euler remarks that it is not at all clear how to solve this PDE system by known methods ('opus maxime arduum').

He then makes a special ansatz: t = ∫J dr + J s, and similarly for the other coordinates, with J, G, H, L, M, N functions of r only. Geometrically X = c(r) + s c'(r) with c' = (J,G,H): the tangent developable of a space curve c, and likewise for the second surface.

On the next page the three conditions reduce to two:
- |c'| = |d'|, so the parameter r measures arc length up to the same factor p.
- |c''| = |d''|; in spherical angles, dm² sin²n + dn² = dμ² sin²ν + dν².

In modern terms, tangent developables of two curves with the same speed and the same curvature function are isometric, whatever their torsion.

In the Adnotatio (next page) Euler observes that such surfaces are necessarily unbounded, so the sphere is not included. He then states that closed surfaces admit no change of shape at all. This is Euler's rigidity conjecture.
errors: No mathematical error on this page; the expansion of rs² and the three conditions are correct.

Gap: the ansatz yields only tangent developables (Gaussian curvature 0), so every solution is also isometric to a plane region. Euler does not remark on this; in that sense the family is a special case of the developable-surface problem.

ideas.what: Condition for isometry of two surfaces under a common parametrization: equality of E, F, G (first fundamental form coefficients), derived from congruence of infinitesimal triangles
ideas.modern_name: First fundamental form / local isometry criterion
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Disquisitiones generales circa superficies curvas, 1827); Euler anticipated parts in E419 (1772)
ideas.where_published: E419 'De solidis quorum superficiem in planum explicare licet' (Novi Comm. 1772) treats the case where one surface is a plane; this fragment (Opera postuma 1862) treats the general two-surface case

ideas.what: Ansatz X = c(r) + s c'(r): tangent developables of two curves with equal arc-length element and equal |c''| are isometric
ideas.modern_name: Isometric deformation of tangent developables (curvature preserved, torsion free)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical 19th-century differential geometry (Monge school / Minding era); unsure of a precise attribution
ideas.where_published: This fragment, Opera postuma I (1862), p. 494-495

ideas.what: Spherical-angle parametrization of the unit tangent, reducing the condition to dm² sin²n + dn² = dμ² sin²ν + dν² (equal arc length of the two tangent indicatrices on the unit sphere)
ideas.modern_name: Tangent indicatrix / curvature as speed of the tangent image
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard; Euler uses similar spherical-image methods elsewhere

ideas.what: Closed surfaces admit no deformation (continued on next page)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (this very fragment, often dated 1766); proved for convex surfaces by Cauchy/Cohn-Vossen, refuted by Connelly 1977
ideas.where_published: This Opera postuma fragment, widely cited (Gluck 1975, Connelly)

missed.claim: The isometry equations for a general pair of surfaces (E=E', F=F', G=G') appear here explicitly, in a fragment that also contains the famous rigidity conjecture. Histories mostly cite this fragment for the rigidity remark rather than for this general bending equation system and the tangent-developable family. This is a minor emphasis issue, not a new result.
missed.quote: in quibus tribus aequationibus continetur solutio nostri problematis. Quemadmodum autem per methodos cognitas iis satisfieri oporteat, neutiquam patet, opusque maxime arduum videtur.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only historiographically, as a pre-Gauss formulation of applicability of arbitrary surfaces; the fragment itself is known.

deep.surprise_reason: This is the well-known Opera postuma fragment on applicable surfaces that contains Euler's rigidity conjecture, widely cited in the rigidity literature. The first-fundamental-form conditions parallel E419. The tangent-developable construction is correct but standard and trivial in hindsight.
transcription_corrections: The letter rendered 'J' in the ansatz t=∫J dr + J s is the printed capital (likely an F/I-type letter in the 1862 font); consistent with the next page, so no change needed.
Header '(Golovin.)' indicates the manuscript source; transcription is otherwise faithful to the image.
